questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Close Readings: Love and Madness
Contested Realities: Debating the Novel
Contemporary World Literatures
Which lives matter? Narratives and experiences of humanity and 'human' lives in Europe
Exile in Slavic Literature

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Close Readings - the course focuses only on Goethe's Faust and Proust's Swann's Way, so you really get to dive deep
Contested Realities - very hard course but ultimately very rewarding - I have never learnt as much in such a short amount of time as I did in this course
Which lives matter - unconventional and creative, a relatively easy course with little preparation but one that really made me think deeply about the topics

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A so-called green tax that you have to pay because the municipality makes sure the trash containers are emptied. It's just over a 100 euros and only some students receive it

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and transportation were more expensive than I thought

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university and their CREA department offer many varying activities every month which are usually free. I also recommend getting a membership at USC where you have access to the gym and a large variety of group classes - or you can sign up for four week course. They have many different sports and activities beyond standard gyms

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can take a trip to Brussels for 20 euros each way and it only takes two hours by train, perfect for a day trip. Other than that, I recommend getting a museum card

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was no problem at all

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My experience was that local students are happy to speak English, so approach them the same way you would anyone else

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dutch people are known for being very honest and straightforward which can feel rude if you are not used to it

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Dutch people are incredibly studious and hard working, which I admire and appreciate

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) If you know someone who has a Dutch bank or you get one yourself, get a museum card - it works for almost all museums in the Netherlands and has paid itself off with three museum visits
2) Depending on your disposition, intro week is not necessarily worth it - you'll likely be exhausted just from the move and the new city, and there's lots of other events and friendly classmates for the rest of the semester
3) If you feel you may need it, attend essay writing workshops through the university. They are free and incredibly helpful. For the few hours I spent attending them, I went from getting Bs to As

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: How open and friendly everyone was as well as learning a lot

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The work load - during my exchange I handed in 10 exams + essay proposals, presentations, sometimes minor weekly assignments on top of the assigned readings. It was rewarding to learn a lot and receive feedback, but the constant examinations were quite stressful

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
